summary: Prior CSRF and forged-cookie findings are fixed. One cleanup gap remains: expiry pruning removes flows but leaves per-flow limiter entries, allowing gradual unbounded growth. One PR race check is also red.
validation: Login now requires strict bootstrap CSRF, same-origin Origin, and JSON content type before credentials are accepted.
Quick Connect status is POST-only with strict CSRF/origin; GET cannot reach authentication or create a session.
Invalid cookies are looked up before per-flow limiter allocation and terminal paths delete limiter entries.
PR checks: one Go race job failed in unrelated discovery test; other Go, build, vulnerability, secret, and artifact jobs passed.
blockers: quickConnectState.prune deletes expired flows but never deletes their quick_connect_poll limiter keys. Abandoned flows can accumulate stale entries across repeated TTL cycles.
Go race CI is not green: TestCanceledAuthoritativeHintDuringInflightReconcileRunsOneFollowup timed out in internal/discovery.
next_action: Route to code: couple expiry pruning with limiter-key cleanup and add an abandoned-flow cleanup test; investigate the failed discovery race check before test stage.

issues.title: Expiry pruning leaks poll limiter entries
issues.details: internal/publicapi/quickconnect.go:quickConnectState.prune removes expired flows from the map but does not remove quick_connect_poll:<idHash> entries. Poll once, abandon 256 flows, wait for TTL, and repeat; limiter memory grows without bound. Couple pruning to limiter cleanup under race-safe ownership and test it.
